purpose: Research evidence and contextual semantics, not a simulation ontology

claims.Claim: Measured é properties are not descriptions of complete residential groups.
claims.Nippur context: TA 184; X 1 / XA 1 retained as catalogued
claims.Secondary interpretation: This return’s reading: Contextual reading of measured plots and fixtures.
claims.Counterevidence/disagreement: Some other uses of é can be broader; no exclusive dictionary definition is proposed.

claims.Claim: Residence can be stated explicitly rather than inferred from an é–person association.
claims.Secondary interpretation: This return’s reading: Relative clause ša ina é ... wašbu supports a residence assertion.
claims.Counterevidence/disagreement: The preceding a-si-rum may be a name; its status interpretation is unresolved.
claims.Generalization limit: Named relation in this account, not a census.

claims.Claim: ḫa-la labels allocations of different kinds, including temporal temple-associated shares.
claims.Period/date: Old Babylonian; Rim-Sin 54 for office division
claims.Secondary interpretation: This return’s reading: Compare objects before selecting “share” or “inheritance portion.”
claims.Counterevidence/disagreement: Undated/damaged plot division does not establish its occasion.
claims.Generalization limit: Not every possible sense of ḫa-la.
claims.Project relevance: Avoids deriving a transaction type from one noun.

claims.Claim: A living father’s division can be combined with conditional heirship and annual support.
claims.Secondary interpretation: This return’s reading: The propositions coexist in the same document.
claims.Counterevidence/disagreement: Damaged obv. 9; actual delivery and broader motives unproved.
claims.Generalization limit: One instrument; not a universal succession regime.
claims.Project relevance: Separates allocation, affiliation, obligation and performance.

claims.Claim: Kinship expressions in affiliation instruments cannot by themselves establish biological relationships.
claims.Secondary interpretation: This return’s reading: Relationships can be constituted or restated within the instrument.
claims.Counterevidence/disagreement: This does not make every patronymic adoptive or fictitious.
claims.Generalization limit: Relation-specific conclusion; not a reconstructed genealogy.
claims.Project relevance: Prevents equating expressed affiliation with biological descent.

claims.Claim: Conditional repudiation clauses are provisions, not evidence that repudiation or its penalty occurred.
claims.Secondary interpretation: This return’s reading: Distinguish condition, sanction and reported event.
claims.Counterevidence/disagreement: Fragmentary texts cannot supply missing outcomes.
claims.Project relevance: Avoids converting legal scenarios into personal biographies.

claims.Claim: A woman’s kinship and deity-linked title can be stated together with a maintenance entitlement.
claims.Secondary interpretation: This return’s reading: nin₉ and LUKUR Ninurta are simultaneous descriptions.
claims.Counterevidence/disagreement: Not all similarly named women are this person.
claims.Generalization limit: One agreement; no citywide rule for titled women.
claims.Project relevance: Shows why kinship, title and entitlement should not be synonyms.

claims.Claim: The maintenance agreement’s alienation restriction does not yield an uncontested modern usufruct category.
claims.Secondary interpretation: Van Wyk 2014 discusses competing readings of whose field is restricted.
claims.Counterevidence/disagreement: Field possessive and legal reconstruction remain disputed.
claims.Project relevance: Preserves uncertainty about the rights involved.

claims.Claim: Annual payment terminology is not confined to remuneration for labor.
claims.Secondary interpretation: This return’s reading: a₂ with annual wording occurs in distinct obligation contexts.
claims.Counterevidence/disagreement: Neither occurrence establishes an employer–employee relation.
claims.Generalization limit: These clauses; no full lexical history of a₂.
claims.Project relevance: Prevents translating all support or rent as wages.

claims.Claim: Receipt language and explicit interest exclusions identify obligations, not a permanent social class.
claims.Secondary interpretation: This return’s reading: šu-ti and máš₂ nu-ub-tuku specify receipt and exclusion of interest.
claims.Counterevidence/disagreement: Catalogue commodity discrepancy in no. 65; no inference of charitable motive.
claims.Project relevance: Separates debtor role, financial terms and personal status.

claims.Claim: A manumission-related instrument distinguishes lifetime service from heirs’ later slave-status claims.
claims.Secondary interpretation: Stone 1987 indexes a freeing; surviving nam-geme₂ and temporal clauses support the distinction.
claims.Counterevidence/disagreement: Release expression restored and queried; marriage/document clause damaged.
claims.Generalization limit: One damaged act; not unrestricted freedom or a general law.
claims.Project relevance: Separates juridical status, duties and time.

claims.Claim: ARAD in a divine seal formula or personal name is insufficient evidence of a person’s slave status.
claims.Secondary interpretation: This return’s reading: Personal-name and devotional uses differ from an explicit status predication.
claims.Counterevidence/disagreement: ARAD can denote human slavery in other contexts; the caution does not erase it.

claims.Claim: Temple-linked rights could be described in temporal portions and transferred.
claims.Secondary interpretation: This return’s reading: Four-month allocations and sales of day-defined entitlements differ from wages.
claims.Counterevidence/disagreement: No proof of actual personal performance or net income.
claims.Generalization limit: These transactions; not every temple office.
claims.Project relevance: Distinguishes rights, rotation, price and work.

claims.Claim: A Nuska-temple office sale combines annual days and an associated field.
